entities.name: Tai Chi multiple falls
observations: In the Atlanta FICSIT randomized trial of 200 community-dwelling adults aged 70+, including 162 women, Tai Chi reduced multiple-fall risk by 47.5% after adjustment for fall-risk factors; fear-of-falling responses improved versus education (P=.046). The abstract did not identify an independent baseline health-indicator predictor.

entities.name: Women Tai Chi indicators
observations: In a 31-woman community Tai Chi pilot, balance performance, functional strength, and mobility improved significantly (P<.05), but balance confidence and fall incidence did not improve.

entities.name: Reactive balance falls
observations: In 125 community-dwelling women aged 65+ followed for one year, posterior single-stepping threshold independently predicted future falls (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.01–2.28; AUC .62); eyes-closed postural sway added predictive value.

entities.name: Older women fall algorithm
observations: In 1,002 community-dwelling women aged 65+ with mild disability, the best fall-prediction algorithm selected prior falls and, in subgroups, balance difficulty while walking, 4-m walking speed, BMI, and knee-extensor strength.

entities.name: Program completer health
observations: Across 10 evidence-based community falls-prevention programs, completers had more fear of falling and lower perceived health at baseline; a higher proportion reduced falls and fear of falling, but sex-specific estimates were unavailable.
